Biological Investigations
The waters beneath the Ross Ice Shelf may contain one of the world's most isolated and unique biomes. The discovery of any life beneath the thick Ross Ice Shelf will be of great scientific interest and could shed considerable light on the life processes taking place in complete and perpetual darkness. Such a discovery would elucidate metabolic activities of the organisms living under the shelf, would provide a means to evaluate the extent to which the plankton and benthic communities beneath the Ross Ice Shelf may be uniquely adapted to their environment, and may allow some understanding of the extent of nutrient flow underneath the shelf. It is possible that novel microbial interactions may occur such as photosynthetic organisms utilizing the light liberated by the luminescent microorganisms or various autotrophic bacteria. The proposed biological-chemical-biochemical studies of the Ross Ice Shelf waters would allow us to determine if and to what extent biological activity is taking place below the ice shelf.
One of the main objectives of the biological programs of RISP is to study the magnitude and extent of interaction between the biota in the water column and sediments in the Ross Sea and those under the Ross Ice Shelf. Eltanin Cruise 51, undertaken on a well coordinated systems approach, was planned to provide data on the physical, chemical, and biological oceanography at the front of the Ross Ice Shelf barrier.
